ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a charged isolated conductor, whose right end contracts into a sharp protruding tip, labeled a; the upper middle is a section of approximately straight surface, labeled b; the left end is a wider, smooth end face, nearby labeled c. Reasoning: When a conductor is in electrostatic equilibrium, the position with larger surface curvature and smaller radius of curvature has greater surface charge density, and the electric field strength outside it is also greater. Point a is the sharpest protruding point, with the smallest radius of curvature; point b is approximately flat, and point c is relatively smooth, rounded, and wide. Therefore, the position where the electric field strength is greatest is point a.

method.method_draft: First identify the local shape at a, b, and c from the image. Compare their radii of curvature: a is the sharpest convex point, b is nearly flat, and c is much more gently rounded/broad. Apply the conductor rule that smaller radius of curvature gives larger surface charge density and therefore larger external electric field. Conclude that the maximum field is at point a.
